fields.label: Apportionment method
fields.value: Massachusetts uses a single sales factor apportionment formula for all business corporations and financial institutions. Multistate business taxable net income is apportioned solely using the sales or receipts factor.
fields.source_citation: TIR 25-5: Tax Provisions in Certain Massachusetts Legislation Enacted in 2024 | Mass.gov

fields.label: Sales sourcing (services and intangibles)
fields.value: Massachusetts uses market-based sourcing for sales other than sales of tangible personal property. Receipts from services are sourced to Massachusetts if delivered to a location in the Commonwealth, and receipts from intangibles are sourced based on use in Massachusetts.

fields.label: Special industry rules
fields.value: Massachusetts provides industry-specific apportionment rules for financial institutions, mutual fund service corporations, airlines, motor carriers, courier and package delivery services, pipeline companies, the electric industry, and the telecommunications industry.
fields.quote: 46, § 37 the Commissioner promulgated industry-specific alternative apportionment regulations for motor carriers, airlines, and courier and package delivery services.

fields.label: Sales/use tax: economic nexus
fields.value: Remote sellers establish economic nexus when Massachusetts sales exceed $100,000 in a calendar year, with no transaction count requirement. The measurement period looks to Massachusetts sales exceeding $100,000 during the preceding calendar year or the current calendar year.
fields.source_citation: 830 CMR 64H.1.9: Remote Retailers and Marketplace Facilitators | Mass.gov

fields.label: Other notable business taxes
fields.value: Massachusetts levies a non-income corporate excise of $2.60 per $1,000 of taxable tangible property or net worth with a $456 minimum excise, but imposes no broad gross receipts tax. Specific gross revenue taxes apply to security corporations at 1.32% or 0.33%, satellite service at 5.0%, and club alcoholic beverages at 0.57%.

fields.label: Individual due date and extension
fields.value: Individual income tax returns are due on April 15 following the close of the tax year. Filers receive an automatic 6-month extension to October 15, provided at least 80% of total tax liability is paid by the original due date.
fields.source_citation: Tax Due Dates and Extensions | Mass.gov
fields.quote: Extensions Personal income tax extensions must be filed on or before April 15, 2026 and will not be accepted after midnight on that date.

fields.label: Pass-through entity tax (PTET)
fields.value: Massachusetts imposes an elective pass-through entity excise under Chapter 63D at a rate of 5.0% on qualified taxable income. Entities elect annually via MassTaxConnect and submit Form 63D-ELT by the underlying return's due date.

fields.label: Composite returns
fields.value: Pass-through entities may file Form MA NRCR on behalf of eligible full-year nonresident members to satisfy their Massachusetts tax obligations. Members must file separately on Form 1-NR/PY if they have other Massachusetts income or exceed the 4% surtax threshold.
fields.source_citation: Tax Guide for Pass-Through Entity Withholding | Mass.gov

fields.label: Key forms
fields.value: Individuals file Form 1 or Form 1-NR/PY, and corporations file Form 355 or Form 355U. Pass-through entities file Form 3, Form 355S, Form 2, Form 63D-ELT, or Form MA NRCR.
fields.quote: An election is made by checking the appropriate box and signing where required on the applicable return (Form 3 for partnerships, Form 355S - Schedule S for S corporations, and Form 2 for trusts).
